concerns.concern: With the authors' own coherence length (~108 nm), the upper critical field is about 28 mT. Measurements extend to 35 mT, so a mixed-state vortex picture contradicts the stated parameters over much of the field range.
concerns.quote: the "mixed state with vortex density → B/Φ₀" picture is inconsistent with the stated parameters over a substantial part of the field range.

concerns.concern: The string thickness (110 nm) is about equal to ξ. Parallel-field vortices nucleate only if the thickness exceeds roughly 2ξ, so vortices may not form at all.
concerns.quote: The authors' parameters place the string at or below this threshold, which directly undermines the central claim.

concerns.concern: The manuscript never explains how a rigid out-of-plane translation of the string in a uniform field displaces pinned vortices relative to their pinning sites, which is needed to produce stiffening.
concerns.quote: The manuscript never explains how out-of-plane translation of a string produces a relative vortex–lattice displacement r.

concerns.concern: The authors' own entry-field formula predicts about 30 vortex entries over the measured window, but only 4–5 jumps per dataset are seen. This contradicts the single-vortex assignment.
concerns.quote: Roughly 30 entries are therefore expected over the measured window, yet only about 4–5 jumps are identified per dataset.

concerns.concern: The expected per-vortex shift (~16 Hz) would be resolvable, so the background should look like a staircase, yet it rises smoothly between jumps. Either the background is not vortex-induced or the single-vortex step size is wrong.
concerns.quote: Either the background is not vortex-induced, or the single-vortex step size is wrong.

concerns.concern: Ω₀ is extracted from a multi-parameter fit, so small changes in critical current or flux offset could appear as fake steps. Raw half-flux frequencies and the fitted circuit parameters versus field must be shown.
concerns.quote: Any small change in I_c or the flux offset ... could appear as a step in fitted Ω₀.

concerns.concern: The smooth ∝B² background could be residual Lorentz-force stiffening, from junction asymmetry or mis-estimated η or L_l. The authors acknowledge this possibility but never exclude it.
concerns.quote: Both produce an artificial ∝B² contribution to Ω₀. The authors acknowledge this possibility in Sec. III but never exclude it.

concerns.concern: Since λ is much larger than both thickness and width, the field penetrates almost uniformly and a 'vortex' does not carry a full flux quantum. Counting vortices via ΔB = Φ₀/(ld) is unjustified.
concerns.quote: A "vortex" in a sample much smaller than λ does not carry a full flux quantum through the cross-section.

concerns.concern: No up/down field-sweep data or trapped-flux tests are shown, although irreversibility is the most basic test of vortex entry and pinning.
concerns.quote: No such data are presented, although this is the most basic test of the interpretation.

concerns.concern: κ_GL > 1/√2 does not by itself imply vortex states when the smallest dimension is ≲ ξ and ≪ λ. Mesoscopic confinement must be considered.
concerns.quote: Satisfying κ_GL > 1/√2 does not by itself imply vortex states in a sample whose smallest dimension is ≲ ξ and ≪ λ.

concerns.concern: The authors should calculate, for example with Ginzburg–Landau simulations of the actual cross-section, whether vortex states are ever energetically favourable below 35 mT.
concerns.quote: whether vortex states are ever energetically favourable below 35 mT.

concerns.concern: In the thin-film limit the relevant critical field is the parallel critical field (~96 mT), not a B_c1/B_c2 mixed-state scenario. The paper should discuss which regime actually applies.
concerns.quote: This is the relevant critical field, not a B_c1/B_c2 mixed-state scenario.

concerns.concern: The in-plane field also acts on the junctions, SQUID leads and CPW. Vortex entry there would alter circuit parameters and produce apparent Ω₀ jumps unrelated to vortices in the string.
concerns.quote: This would produce apparent Ω₀ jumps unrelated to vortices in the string.

concerns.concern: Vortex entry into the string, which is part of the SQUID loop, should cause correlated jumps in cavity frequency, flux offset or decay rate. These already-available data are not reported.
concerns.quote: Correlated jumps in ω_c(Φ_b), φ_off, or κ would be strong independent evidence, and the authors already have these data.

concerns.concern: Field misalignment creates an out-of-plane component that can nucleate vortices in the wide CPW and ground planes. Alignment accuracy and any compensation procedure are not reported.
concerns.quote: The alignment accuracy and any compensation procedure must be reported.

concerns.concern: Sweeping the out-of-plane field over a full SQUID period at every in-plane field point may itself cause flux entry, exit or rearrangement, producing stochastic jumps.
concerns.quote: This is a likely source of stochastic, history-dependent jumps.

concerns.concern: Temperature is never varied, although the Labusch parameter and Campbell response should depend on T and vanish at T_c. This would discriminate vortex effects from artifacts.
concerns.quote: α_L(B, T) appears in Eq. (8), but T is never varied.

concerns.concern: No direct superconducting characterization of the string is provided: no T_c, critical field or transport data. This is needed for a claim of type-II behaviour in nominally type-I Al.
concerns.quote: A paper whose main claim rests on type-II behaviour of a nominally type-I material needs at least one direct measurement.

concerns.concern: Eq. (8) should use the material density (2700 kg/m³), not an effective density of 910 kg/m³ obtained from modal mass over full volume. This underestimates α_L by about 3×.
concerns.quote: This is inconsistent and underestimates α_L and Δα_L by about 3×.

concerns.concern: Eq. (6) and the Likharev/Stan expressions were derived for thin strips in perpendicular fields. Substituting the thickness for a parallel-field geometry is unjustified.
concerns.quote: Substituting the thickness d for a parallel-field geometry is not justified.

concerns.concern: Eq. (7), taken from a treatment of Pearl vortices in narrow strips in perpendicular fields, is applied to in-plane vortices without justification or re-derivation.
concerns.quote: Its use for in-plane vortices in the l × d cross-section requires justification or a re-derivation.

concerns.concern: B_c1 ≈ 5 mT is chosen from an 'onset' in Fig. 2(d), but the data start at ~6 mT and the fit function has no threshold. The data therefore give no evidence for an onset.
concerns.quote: The fit A₀ + C·B^k contains no threshold, so the data provide no evidence for an onset at all.

concerns.concern: If α_L came from vortices with the density of Eq. (7), it should vanish below B_c1 and follow a specific structure above it. Instead, a threshold-free power law is fitted.
concerns.quote: The model actually fitted to the data should be stated.

concerns.concern: Attributing the more than fivefold gap between the empirical entry field and its upper bound to disorder and edge roughness, without independent checks, makes the argument unfalsifiable.
concerns.quote: Attributing this gap to "disorder and edge roughness" without any independent check makes the argument unfalsifiable.

concerns.concern: If coupling is via tilt, it depends on the local slope, which vanishes at the antinode and peaks near the clamps. It is therefore non-uniform and possibly tiny, and its magnitude must be estimated.
concerns.quote: the coupling is neither "uniform" nor described by Eq. (8).

concerns.concern: In standard vibrating-reed theory the near-B² shift comes from magnetic line tension. Directly identifying the density-weighted frequency shift with α_L is non-standard and needs derivation.
concerns.quote: Identifying ρ_eff Δ(Ω²) directly with α_L is not the standard relation and needs a derivation.

concerns.concern: The Campbell length implied by the reported α_L is of order a micrometre, much larger than the sample dimensions, so the response is not pinning-dominated in the usual sense. This is never discussed.
concerns.quote: λ_C is of order a micrometre, much larger than d and w.

concerns.concern: Uniform pinning with constant per-vortex stiffness predicts exponent k = 1, not 1.81, and the extracted stiffness is field dependent. The two supporting statements contradict each other.
concerns.quote: The two statements are mutually inconsistent and should not both be presented as supporting the picture.

concerns.concern: The exponent k is fitted over less than a decade in field with three free parameters. It is likely correlated with A₀ and indistinguishable from 2; the covariance should be reported and k = 2 tested.
concerns.quote: The covariance should be reported, and k = 2 tested explicitly.

concerns.concern: No theoretical prediction supports k = 1.81. The cited bulk works do not predict it, and essentially any exponent between 1 and 2 could be rationalized.
concerns.quote: In this geometry, essentially any exponent between 1 and 2 could be rationalized.

concerns.concern: The same k = 1.81 ± 0.05 is quoted for several datasets and independent cooldowns. It is unclear whether this is a global fit and whether the jumps were included.
concerns.quote: why independent cooldowns with different jump positions give identical exponents.

concerns.concern: Superconducting magnetostriction and field-dependent free-energy effects (Meissner diamagnetic energy, kinetic inductance) also give smooth near-B² frequency shifts and are not considered.
concerns.quote: Both produce smooth near-B² frequency shifts and are not considered.

concerns.concern: Dismissing the volume effect by equating ΔΩ/Ω with the relative volume change ignores stress amplification in a high-stress string and the large core volume fraction. A proper estimate is needed.
concerns.quote: A proper estimate is needed, even if it ultimately still rules the mechanism out.

concerns.concern: The extracted Ω₀ depends on the circuit model (Eq. (A1) vs Eq. (3)), yet the same exponent is reported for both. A side-by-side comparison on the same data, with residuals, is needed.
concerns.quote: A side-by-side comparison on the same data, with residuals, is needed.

concerns.concern: The steps are comparable to the linewidth and error bars, so several are only 2–3σ. No objective change-point detection or significance criterion is described.
concerns.quote: No objective change-point detection or significance criterion is described, and the arrows appear to be placed by eye.

concerns.concern: Resolvability of stiffness steps is governed by frequency noise (Allan deviation), not thermal force PSD. Frequency-stability data should be shown.
concerns.quote: Thermal force PSD is not the relevant metric, and the frequency-stability data should be shown.

concerns.concern: Amplifier imprecision noise likely dominates over thermal force noise. The assumed 85 mK mode temperature is not verified by calibrated thermal-noise measurements.
concerns.quote: The mode temperature (assumed 85 mK in x_rms) is not verified against a calibrated thermal-noise area versus fridge temperature.

concerns.concern: Sub-unity cooperativity does not rule out 10 Hz-level optical-spring shifts from SQUID Kerr nonlinearity or detuning. These could vary systematically with field.
concerns.quote: Sub-unity cooperativity does not guarantee negligible frequency shifts at the 10 Hz level, half a linewidth.

concerns.concern: The text alternates between 'one or a few flux quanta' and 'a single vortex'. The single-vortex pinning energies may be overestimated several-fold.
concerns.quote: The quantitative single-vortex pinning energies depend on this choice and may be overestimated several-fold.

concerns.concern: A single vortex's contribution is weighted by the mode shape at its unknown position, varying from 0 to 2. Eq. (9) neglects this, adding at least that factor of uncertainty to the per-vortex stiffness.
concerns.quote: Eq. (9) and k_p ≈ AΔα_L neglect it.

concerns.concern: Double-layer shadow evaporation may give two Al layers separated by AlOx, each much thinner than 110 nm. This would change the vortex physics qualitatively, so the layer stack must be specified.
concerns.quote: The layer stack of the string should be specified.

concerns.concern: The mean free path is set to an assumed ~10 nm grain size with no measurement, yet all derived superconducting lengths and fields scale with it. Resistivity, RRR, T_c or critical-field data are needed.
concerns.quote: All downstream quantities (ξ, λ, κ, B_c1) scale with this guess.

concerns.concern: The dirty-limit penetration-depth formula is misapplied (1.33 used as a multiplicative prefactor). The standard formula gives λ ≈ 550 nm rather than 840 nm, which also changes κ_GL.
concerns.quote: With the standard formula, λ ≈ 550 nm rather than 840 nm, and κ_GL changes accordingly.

concerns.concern: The quoted effective mass (0.6 pg) is inconsistent with the nominal geometry (~0.9 pg). This implies different real dimensions or composition, which would change the vortex estimates.
concerns.quote: The quoted m_eff = 0.6 pg implies smaller real dimensions or a different composition, which would also change d and the vortex estimates.

concerns.concern: The caveat that values are estimates is not followed by uncertainty propagation. Plausible mean-free-path ranges change the critical fields and the vortex-existence criterion by factors of several.
concerns.quote: The statement that "quoted values should be regarded as estimates" is not followed by uncertainty propagation.

concerns.concern: The field-cooled threshold is described as screening that enhances the Bean–Livingston barrier. However, no screening currents arise under field cooling, and the Likharev/Stan criterion is a thermodynamic stability threshold, not a barrier enhancement.
concerns.quote: Under field cooling no screening currents are set up.

concerns.concern: A field-cooled threshold ten times larger than the zero-field-cooled entry field reverses the usual relationship.
concerns.quote: an FC threshold ten times larger than the ZFC entry field is the reverse of the usual relationship.

concerns.concern: Observed jump spacings (1.5–5 mT) exceed the predicted 0.63–1.25 mT. The unquantified edge-roughness explanation could rationalize any spacing.
concerns.quote: is not quantified and could rationalize any spacing.

concerns.concern: In parallel geometry the barrier-relevant surfaces are the top and bottom faces, not the lateral edges. The discussion of edge-mediated entry should be reconsidered.
concerns.quote: the barrier-relevant surfaces are the top and bottom faces (separated by d), not the lateral "edges" of the strip.

concerns.concern: The authors discuss field-cooled versus zero-field-cooled thresholds but show no field-cooled measurement, under which α_L should differ markedly.
concerns.quote: The authors themselves discuss FC versus ZFC entry thresholds, yet no FC measurement is shown.

concerns.concern: Rotating the in-plane field parallel to the string, which changes vortex geometry while removing Lorentz-force coupling, would cleanly separate the mechanisms but was not done.
concerns.quote: This would separate the mechanisms cleanly.

concerns.concern: The mechanical damping versus field is not reported, although vortex viscosity and creep should change it and it is available from the same spectra.
concerns.quote: Γ_m(B_ip) is not reported, although it is available from the same spectra and would be a key signature.

concerns.concern: Only one device is studied. Control devices, such as strings of different thickness or a loop without a string, are needed.
concerns.quote: Only a single device is studied.

concerns.concern: No fixed-field time traces showing switching or telegraph noise are presented, so the 'real-time' and 'spontaneous flux dynamics' claims are unsupported.
concerns.quote: Without time traces, the "real-time" and "spontaneous flux dynamics" claims in Sec. V are unsupported.

concerns.concern: Slow frequency drift and instrumental events (e.g., magnet supply range switching) are not excluded as sources of the steps. Correlations with time stamps should be checked.
concerns.quote: A 10–50 Hz step could also coincide with instrumental events such as magnet supply range switching.

concerns.concern: A jump at ≈22.5 mT appears in both cooldowns, which conflicts with the claimed stochasticity and may indicate a deterministic or instrumental origin.
concerns.quote: This is somewhat at odds with the claimed stochasticity and could indicate a deterministic or instrumental origin.

concerns.concern: Frequency steps could arise from avoided crossings with other mechanical modes, or from coupling to field-tunable TLS or spin defects. These are not discussed.
concerns.quote: Frequency steps could also arise from avoided crossings with other mechanical modes, or from coupling to field-tunable TLS or spin defects.

concerns.concern: Because the pinning range is comparable to the film thickness, the restoring force may reflect geometric confinement or surface barriers rather than defect pinning.
concerns.quote: the term "pinning energy" may be a misnomer.

concerns.concern: The pinning energy extrapolates a harmonic curvature out to ξ and is uncertain by at least an order of magnitude. It should be compared with a condensation-energy estimate.
concerns.quote: the result is uncertain by at least an order of magnitude.

concerns.concern: The 'attonewton-scale forces' are Δk·x_rms, not a measured force, and comparing them with thermal force noise is a category error. The abstract claim is misleading.
concerns.quote: No vortex-exerted force is measured: the observable is a stiffness or frequency change.

concerns.concern: Absolute α_L relies on extrapolating the power law to zero field, since data are referenced to 20 or 35 mT. It should be stated whether Ω₀ at zero field was measured.
concerns.quote: It should be stated whether Ω₀ at B = 0 was measured.

concerns.concern: The quoted per-vortex stiffness range of 10–20 N/m² does not follow from the inset α_L values, which give about 4–12 N/m².
concerns.quote: The quoted range "10–20 N m⁻²" does not follow from the stated numbers.

concerns.concern: α_L is defined per unit vortex length (units N/m²) but quoted in N/m⁴. The definitions are inconsistent.
concerns.quote: The definitions should be made consistent.

concerns.concern: Using the wrong effective density in Eq. (9) carries the factor-of-3 error into Δα_L and the per-vortex pinning stiffness.
concerns.quote: propagates the factor-3 error of item 30 into Δα_L and k_p.

concerns.concern: The claimed consistency with macro-scale vibrating-reed measurements is unsupported by any specific material, value or Al reference, and cross-material comparison is not meaningful.
concerns.quote: Comparing pinning strengths across very different materials is not meaningful.

concerns.concern: Comparing the pinning energy with k_BT is uninformative. Thermal activation rates over the measurement time, or the depinning current, would be meaningful.
concerns.quote: U ≫ k_BT (≈7 µeV) is not informative.

concerns.concern: The two 'successive' datasets in Fig. 3(a) cover non-overlapping field ranges, so reproducibility within a cooldown cannot be assessed, and their run order is unclear.
concerns.quote: Reproducibility within a cooldown therefore cannot be assessed, and the run order of "Dataset 1" and "Dataset 2" is unclear.

concerns.concern: Stochastic, history-dependent behaviour is claimed from only three partially overlapping sweeps. Many repeated sweeps are needed to establish jump statistics.
concerns.quote: Many repeated sweeps over the same field range are needed to establish the jump statistics.

concerns.concern: VNA-driven and thermal-noise data are mixed. The method behind each point and possible systematic offsets between methods should be stated and quantified.
concerns.quote: Which points come from which method should be stated, and possible systematic offsets between the two ... should be quantified.

concerns.concern: Values of the single-photon coupling, intracavity photon number and cooperativity are not given for each field.
concerns.quote: "C < 1" should be backed by numbers for each B_ip.

concerns.concern: Error bars in Figs. 3 and 4 are undefined, and fit residuals for Eq. (3) are never shown, so fit quality cannot be judged.
concerns.quote: Fit residuals for Eq. (3) are never shown, so fit quality cannot be judged.

concerns.concern: Fig. 2(c) seems to show half-flux endpoints closer together than the Ω₀ spread implied by Fig. 2(d). This needs clarification.
concerns.quote: it should be clarified because Ω₀ is supposed to be observable directly there.

concerns.concern: The SQUID model uses the applied rather than the self-consistent flux. Screening (β_L ≈ 0.17) is not negligible and should be included or bounded.
concerns.quote: Screening should be included, or its effect bounded.

concerns.concern: The initial mode-shape factor η = 0.9 differs from 2/π for a sinusoidal mode. It is unclear whether η is fixed or free and how it trades off with Ω₀.
concerns.quote: It should be stated whether η is fixed or free, and how it trades off with Ω₀.

concerns.concern: The coupling formula uses the total field B, whereas the relevant component for out-of-plane displacement is B_ip.
concerns.quote: the relevant component for out-of-plane displacement is B_ip. This should be clarified.

concerns.concern: The '0.25 mT resolution' is just the step size. Actual field accuracy, calibration and magnet remanence should be stated, especially given the claimed ZFC conditions.
concerns.quote: The actual field accuracy, calibration, and remanence of the magnet should be stated, especially since ZFC conditions are claimed.

concerns.concern: A double-sided force PSD is used, and consistency of the bandwidth integration with this convention should be checked.
concerns.quote: Whether the bandwidth integration of 1–10 Hz is consistent with this convention should be checked.

concerns.concern: All lengths are quoted at T = 0. This should be stated explicitly given the self-heating and mode-temperature questions.
concerns.quote: the self-heating and mode-temperature questions below make it worth stating explicitly.

concerns.concern: The 1600 nm value is the BCS/Pippard coherence length ξ₀, not a GL length, and the notation obscures which formulas are applied.
concerns.quote: The notation obscures which formulas are being applied.

concerns.concern: Claims of mapping the disorder landscape and identifying decoherence pathways are unsupported, since no spatial information or qubit metric is obtained.
concerns.quote: No spatial information is obtained, and no qubit-relevant metric is measured.

concerns.concern: In-situ mechanical determination of B_c1 and B_c2 is claimed but not shown: B_c1 is assumed from a fit, and B_c2 is never reached.
concerns.quote: B_c1 is assumed from a fit, and B_c2 is never reached or identified.

concerns.concern: Statements about progress toward single-photon strong coupling are not backed by coupling-rate numbers.
concerns.quote: not backed by any coupling-rate numbers in this work.

concerns.concern: Many derived numbers are given with false precision while the inputs are uncertain by factors of 2–10. A consistent uncertainty budget is needed.
concerns.quote: A consistent uncertainty budget is needed for every quantitative claim.

concerns.concern: Two key assumptions appear only as footnotes, negligible Meissner field enhancement and symmetric junctions, though both affect Ω₀ extraction. They should be justified in the main text.
concerns.quote: Both directly affect the extraction of Ω₀ and should be justified in the main text.

concerns.concern: Symbols are overloaded: α has three meanings, κ means both cavity decay and the GL parameter, and ϑ and C denote the same quantity.
concerns.quote: κ denotes both cavity decay and the GL parameter.

concerns.concern: There are notation inconsistencies: 'L₁/2' in Fig. 1(b) versus L_l in the text, undefined S₀(Φ_b), and loose use of Ω_m versus Ω₀ in Eq. (9).
concerns.quote: S₀(Φ_b) in Eq. (A1) is undefined.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 4 caption mismatches the plot (blue vs green markers; black squares vs filled circles).
concerns.quote: The caption describes "blue circles," but the plotted data are green.

concerns.concern: It is unclear whether the previous data in Fig. 4 were refitted with Eq. (3) or retain the Eq. (A1) analysis.
concerns.quote: unclear whether the previous data were refitted with Eq. (3) or retain the Eq. (A1) analysis.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 1(c) schematic does not clearly show vortex orientation relative to the string dimensions and field, on which the argument hinges.
concerns.quote: the figure should make this explicit.

concerns.concern: Fig. 2(d) is said to be fitted with Eq. (3), but its data appear to come from Ref. 46, which used Eq. (A1).
concerns.quote: Fig. 2(d) is said to be fitted with Eq. (3), but the data appear to be from Ref. 46, which used Eq. (A1).

concerns.concern: Several references are duplicated (Stan et al., Kober et al., Foltyn et al.), and one is mis-cited.
concerns.quote: Refs. 34 and 70 are identical (Stan et al., PRL 92, 097003).

concerns.concern: Several references are incomplete or misspelled, and the 1.33 factor is attributed to an arXiv preprint instead of its standard textbook source.
concerns.quote: The α = 1.33 factor is attributed to an arXiv preprint (Ref. 61) rather than to its standard textbook source.
